newsitem.title: USA: USDA pegs Brazil 97/8 coffee crop at 28 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: USDA pegs Brazil 97/8 coffee crop at 28 mln bags.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department on Friday forecast Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop at 28.0 million 60-kilogram bags, up from a revised 27.5 million bags seen for 1996/97.
In its World Agricultural Production report, USDA pegged Colombia's 1997/98 coffee at 11.3 million bags, up from a sharply revised estimate of 10.3 million bags for 1996/97.
It previously forecast the Colombia 1996/97 coffee crop at 12.5 million bags.

In its first forecast for 1997/98, USDA pegged world coffee production at 103.7 million bags, up from revised 100.7 million bags last season. The department said output in 1997/98 would match the previous record crop produced in 1991/92.

On Brazil, USDA said its forecast included 23 million bags of Arabica and five million bags of Robusta. It said a number of factors, including favorable growing conditions, higher prices and increased area, contributed to the bigger 1997/98 crop.
USDA officials surveyed Brazil coffee producing regions in September 1996 and again in March and April of this year.

USDA said the total number of Brazil coffee trees is forecast at 3.6 billion, up five percent from the 1996/97 season. Brazil's coffee production potential is currently estimated at 35 million bags, it said.

USDA said it revised down its forecast for Colombia 1996/97 coffee output to the smallest in 20 years due to unusually heavy rains that damaged coffee flowering, insect damage, aging trees and loss of coffee lands to other crops. Lower prices also took a toll as producers reduced efforts cultivating the crops, it said.
USDA said its 1996/97 Colombia coffee estimate took into account high production levels reported by the Colombia Coffee Growers Federation during April and May.
"Colombian coffee production for the near future is expected to fluctuate between 11 and 13 million bags," USDA said in the semi-annual look at world coffee production.
"Improved yield levels are projected to offset reduced area. Once coffee prices weaken again, the downward trend in area is likely to resume," it added.
The department said due to dramatically improved prices since February, growers have regained enthusiasm for the crop which should result in better cultivation this year.
USDA's forecast of the 1997/98 Brazil crop exceeded market expectations by about a million bags. Its world projection also outstripped trade forecasts for about 100 million bags.
